newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly jobless claims edge higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly jobless claims edge higher.

text.p: The number of Americans claiming first-time unemployment benefits rose slightly last week, the government said Thursday.
The Labour Department said initial claims edged up to 314,000 in the week ended March 29 from 313,000 the week before. Wall Street economists had expected 310,000 claims.
The four-week moving average, which is viewed as a more accurate indicator than the more-volatile weekly figures, also rose slightly. It stood it 312,500 last week, up from 312,000 the week earlier.

The total number of Americans continuing to collect jobless benefits fell by 10,000 to 2.3 million in the week ended March 22, the latest period for which those data were available. That was the lowest level since Dec. 23, 1989, when continued claims hit 2,291,000, the department said.
The previous week's continued claims data were revised upward to 2,310,000.

The department said three states reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the latest week. They were Tennessee, with 2,468 fewer filings; Oregon, with 1,596; and New York, with 1,220.
Tennessee reported fewer layoffs in the food, apparel, trade and service industries and in agriculture. Oregon and New York gave no reasons for the reduced filings.
Three states reported increases in claims exceeding 1,000. They were Maryland, with 2,608 additional filings; Louisiana, with 1,847; and Ohio, with 1,114.

Maryland said it had layoffs in the fabricated metals, transportation equipment, publishing, optical goods and service industries. Louisiana and Ohio both reported layoffs in the transportation equipment industry.
